Elected tsar of Russia by the Seven Boyars in 1610 — though he never took that throne — this eldest son of Sigismund III went on to rule Poland and Lithuania; who is he?
Władysław IV Vasa: Ruler of Poland–Lithuania from 1632 to 1648.
China's premier through the 1980s, he was the architect of political reform — until his support for the 1989 Tiananmen Square protests cost him all his power. Who is this fallen reformer?
Who among these was born first?
Patrick Geddes (born 1854) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Omar Khayyam (born 1048) is the earliest of the four.
Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these was founded earliest?
MUMPS (founded 1966) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below is best known as a physicist?
John Archibald Wheeler is a physicist. John Archibald Wheeler (July 9, 1911 – April 13, 2008) was an American theoretical physicist.
Pick the mathematician from these four.
Émilie du Châtelet is a mathematician. It circulated widely, generated heated debates, and was translated into German and Italian in 1743.
What is the atomic number of Darmstadtium?
Darmstadtium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Ds and atomic number 110.
What is the atomic number of Gold?
Gold is a chemical element; its chemical symbol is Au (from Latin aurum) and atomic number 79.
In what year did Kitty Oppenheimer die?
Kitty Oppenheimer: Robert Oppenheimer, the director of the Manhattan Project's Los Alamos Laboratory during World War II.
In what year was Boron discovered?
Boron is a chemical element; it has symbol B and atomic number 5.
Dopamine: Pfizer. Dopamine (DA, a contraction of 3,4-dihydroxyphenethylamine) is a neuromodulatory molecule that plays several important roles in cells.
In which country is TAI TF Kaan?
TAI TF Kaan: Turkey. Designed to replace the Turkish Air Force’s fleet of F-16 Fighting Falcons, the Kaan is also intended for export to international markets.
Who is credited with discovering Apus?
Apus: Petrus Plancius. Apus is a small constellation in the southern sky.
Who is credited with discovering Cat's Eye Nebula?
Cat's Eye Nebula: William Herschel. It is a well-studied object that has been observed from radio to X-ray wavelengths.
Who is credited with discovering Hydrogen?
Hydrogen: Henry Cavendish. Hydrogen is a chemical element; it has the symbol H and atomic number 1.
Who is credited with discovering Astatine?
Astatine: Emilio G. Segrè. Astatine is a chemical element; it has symbol At and atomic number 85.

Born into a prominent Stockholm family, this fluent-in-six-languages inventor filed his first patent at 24 and went on to hold 355 in all, while owning the arms-and-engineering firm Bofors. Who was he?
Alfred Nobel (noh-BEL; 21 October 1833 - 10 December 1896) was a Swedish chemist, inventor, engineer, and businessman.

Native to tropical America and carried across the Pacific by Spanish traders aboard the Manila galleons, this small tree in the same family as soursop produces a scaly-skinned fruit with sweet, creamy flesh — what's the species?
Annona squamosa is a small, well-branched tree or shrub from the family Annonaceae that bears edible fruits called sugar apples or sweetsops or custard apples.
This genus of roughly 300 evergreen flowering plants includes one edible species enjoyed as a vegetable and another grown purely as an ornamental — which genus?
Asparagus (genus) is a genus of flowering plants in the family Asparagaceae, subfamily Asparagoideae.

Found naturally in many plants and abbreviated "Bz," this white crystalline compound is the simplest of the aromatic carboxylic acids and lends its salts to the world of food preservatives — what is it?
Benzoic acid is a white or colorless crystalline organic compound with the formula C6H5COOH, whose structure consists of a benzene ring (C6H6) with a carboxyl (C(=O)OH) substituent.
Every subatomic particle is either this integer-spin class or a fermion; Paul Dirac named the class after physicist Satyendra Nath Bose, whose statistics they obey — what's the class called?
Boson is a subatomic particle whose spin quantum number has an integer value (0, 1, 2,...).
With the chemical formula CaO, this white, caustic, alkaline solid is produced by heating limestone and has been used since antiquity in construction and agriculture — what's the compound's name?
Calcium oxide (formula: CaO), commonly known as quicklime or burnt lime, is a widely used chemical compound.
Their name is Greek for "head-feet," and fishers sometimes call them "inkfish" for their ink-squirting trick; squid, octopus and nautilus all belong. What's this molluscan class?
Cephalopod is any member of the molluscan class Cephalopoda (Greek plural, kephalpodes; "head-feet") such as a squid, octopus, cuttlefish, or nautilus.
After serving as dean of Harvard's Faculty of Arts and Sciences, this political scientist became the university's 30th president in July 2023 — who is she?
Claudine Gay (born August 4, 1970) is an American political scientist who is the Wilbur A. Cowett Professor of Government and of African and African-American Studies at Harvard University.
This group of related RNA viruses causes respiratory illnesses ranging from the mild common cold to deadly diseases like SARS, MERS, and COVID-19 — what's this virus family called?
Coronavirus are a group of related RNA viruses that cause diseases in mammals and birds.
Known mostly through DNA evidence rather than abundant fossils, this extinct group of archaic humans ranged across Asia between roughly 200,000 and 32,000 years ago — what are they called?
Denisovan (d-(nz)) are an extinct species or subspecies of archaic human that ranged across Asia during the Middle to Late Pleistocene, approximately 200,000-32,000 years ago.

This hypothetical megastructure would encircle an entire star to capture most of its energy output, conceived as a thought experiment for how an advanced civilization might meet growing power needs — what's the concept called?
Dyson sphere is a hypothetical megastructure that encompasses a star and captures a large percentage of its power output.

This genus's tapering spacing of stem nodes toward the tip is credited with inspiring John Napier's work on logarithms; today it's the sole living genus of an ancient, spore-producing plant lineage nicknamed horsetail — which genus?
Equisetum (horsetail) is the only living genus in Equisetaceae, a family of vascular plants that reproduce by spores rather than seeds.
Also badged as the Citroën Jumper and the Peugeot Boxer in Europe, this light commercial van entered North America in 2014 as the Ram ProMaster — which van?
Fiat Ducato is a light commercial vehicle jointly developed by FCA Italy and PSA Group (now Stellantis), and mainly manufactured by Sevel, a joint venture between the two companies since 1981.

This Austrian engineer founded a firearms company in 1963; when his first pistol entered Austrian service in 1982, its famous model number referred to his 17th patent, not the rounds it held — who is he?
Prince Carl Philip, Duke of Värmland
Gaston Glock (19 July 1929 - 27 December 2023) was an Austrian engineer and businessman.
What common name covers a diverse family of marine ray-finned fish in the order Perciformes, most belonging to the genera Epinephelus or Mycteroperca?
Grouper are a diverse group of marine ray-finned fish in the family Epinephelidae, in the order Perciformes.
Named after the physicist who first proved the existence of electromagnetic waves, this SI unit measures one cycle per second. What unit is it?
Hertz (symbol: Hz) is the unit of frequency in the International System of Units (SI), often described as being equivalent to one event (or cycle) per second.

Ranging from mild headaches and poor balance to severe confusion and seizures, this low-blood-sodium condition can be triggered by causes as varied as vomiting, diuretics, or overhydration — what's it called?
Hyponatremia is a low concentration of sodium in the blood. It is generally defined as a sodium concentration of less than 135 mmol/L (135 mEq/L), with severe hyponatremia being below 120 mEq/L.
Serving as president of the European Commission from 1985 to 1995, this French politician played a central role in creating the European single market and laying groundwork for the euro — who is he?
Jacques Delors (20 July 1925 - 27 December 2023) was a French politician who served as president of the European Commission from 1985 to 1995.

An evergreen conifer in the cypress family, this small tree or shrub boasts the largest geographical range of any woody plant on Earth, spanning the cool temperate Northern Hemisphere — which species?
Juniperus communis is a species of small tree or shrub in the cypress family Cupressaceae.

Amphoteric and unreactive, this post-transition metal reacts with both acids and bases, melts at a low temperature, and tarnishes from shiny to dull gray in air — and three of its isotopes end major nuclear decay chains. Which element is it?
Lead is a chemical element with the symbol Pb (from the Latin plumbum) and atomic number 82.
Based on a commercial airliner design, this four-engine turboprop aircraft hunts submarines for the U.S. Navy using a distinctive tail-mounted magnetic detector — what plane is it?
Lockheed P-3 Orion is a four-engined, turboprop anti-submarine and maritime surveillance aircraft developed for the United States Navy and introduced in the 1960s.

With over 2,400 species sporting triangular heads, bulging eyes on flexible necks, and folded forelegs built to snatch prey, these insects count termites and cockroaches among their closest relatives — what are they?
Mantis are an order (Mantodea) of insects that contains over 2,400 species in about 460 genera in 33 families.
This medication treats nausea, vomiting, and acid reflux by blocking dopamine receptors, but is rarely recommended for more than twelve weeks due to a risk of movement disorders — what drug is it?
Metoclopramide is a medication used to treat nausea, vomiting, gastroparesis, and gastroesophageal reflux disease.
This small green legume, cultivated widely across East and South Asia, is used in both savory dishes and sweet desserts — what is it?
Mung bean (Vigna radiata) is a plant species in the legume family.

Found across 26 African countries in lakes, rivers and swamps — with one of its largest undisturbed populations at Kenya's Lake Turkana — adult males of this reptile can stretch past five meters; what is it?
Nile crocodile (Crocodylus niloticus) is a large crocodilian native to freshwater habitats in Africa, where it is present in 26 countries.
Named from the Greek word for 'smell,' this hard, brittle, bluish-white transition metal has the highest density of any stable element and is often alloyed for fountain pen nib tips — which element?
Osmium (from Ancient Greek (osm) 'smell') is a chemical element; it has symbol Os and atomic number 76.
Commercially produced from citrus fruits as a white-to-light-brown powder, this plant-cell-wall polysaccharide is the gelling agent that makes jams and jellies set — what is it?
Pectin (Ancient) is a heteropolysaccharide, a structural polymer contained in the cell walls and middle lamellae of terrestrial plants.
Confirming and popularizing Isaac Newton's work, this French scholar authored the five-volume 'Mécanique céleste' and helped pioneer the Bayesian view of probability — who is he?

Pierre-Simon Laplace (23 March 1749 - 5 March 1827) was a French polymath, a scholar whose work has been instrumental in the fields of physics, astronomy, mathematics, engineering, statistics, and philosophy.
Legally defined as exactly 0.45359237 kilograms and divided into 16 avoirdupois ounces, this unit of mass is used in both British imperial and U.S. customary systems — what is it?
Pound (mass) is a unit of mass used in both the British imperial and United States customary systems of measurement.
Used to treat malaria and babesiosis, this medication also gives tonic water its distinctive bitter taste — what is it?
Quinine is a medication used to treat malaria and babesiosis. While sometimes used for nocturnal leg cramps, quinine is not recommended for this purpose due to the risk of serious side effects.
A Jesuit priest, poet, and diplomat from the Republic of Ragusa, this polymath produced an early precursor of atomic theory and in 1753 discovered the Moon has no atmosphere — who was he?
Roger Joseph Boscovich (18 May 1711 - 13 February 1787) was a physicist, astronomer, mathematician, philosopher, diplomat, poet, theologian, Jesuit priest, and a polymath from the Republic of Ragusa.

After early attempts at family-friendly Christian video games found little success, this American developer switched to horror in 2014 and created a hit franchise about animatronic mascots that come alive at night — who is he?

Scott Cawthon (born June 4, 1978) is an American video game developer, writer, and producer best known for creating Five Nights at Freddy's, a series of horror video games which expanded into a media franchise.
Famous for their slowness, these tree-dwelling Neotropical mammals are closest relatives of anteaters and come in just seven living species across two genera — what are they?
Sloth are a Neotropical group of xenarthran mammals constituting the suborder Folivora, including the extant arboreal tree sloths and extinct terrestrial ground sloths.
Innervated by the accessory nerve, which of the body's largest and most superficial neck structures rotates the head to the opposite side and flexes the neck?
Sternocleidomastoid muscle is one of the largest and most superficial cervical muscles.

Known for a leather-like smell when freshly milled and prized for durability and water resistance, this tropical hardwood tree bears small, fragrant white flowers and large, papery, often-hairy leaves — name this tree?
Teak (Tectona grandis) is a tropical hardwood tree species in the family Lamiaceae.
This muscular organ in the mouth manipulates food for chewing and swallowing, serves as the body's primary organ of taste, and also enables human speech — what organ is it?
Tongue is a muscular organ in the mouth of a typical tetrapod.
Native to Europe and southwestern Asia, this herbaceous perennial flowering plant is the type species of its genus and a member of the honeysuckle family — which herb?
Valerian (herb) (Valeriana officinalis) is an herbaceous perennial flowering plant in the family Caprifoliaceae, native to Europe and southwestern Asia.
This Austrian physicist earned a 1945 Nobel Prize for the exclusion principle and, in 1930, proposed the existence of what would become known as the neutrino — who is he?
Wolfgang Pauli (25 April 1900 - 15 December 1958) was an Austrian theoretical physicist and a pioneer of quantum mechanics.

Introduced to the British Isles by 1500 and known there simply as 'sycamore,' this wind-tolerant maple from Central Europe can grow to 35 metres and has turned invasive in North America and Australia — which species?
Acer pseudoplatanus: Species of maple tree. It is a large deciduous, broad-leaved tree, tolerant of wind and coastal exposure.
Launched to challenge the Boeing 747, this is the world's largest passenger airliner and the only full-length double-deck jet — which aircraft, unveiled in Toulouse in 2005?
This mushroom genus contains the notorious 'death cap,' responsible for roughly 90% of all fatal mushroom poisonings worldwide — which genus?
Amanita: Genus of mushrooms. The genus is responsible for 95% of fatalities resulting from mushroom poisoning, with the death cap accounting for 90% of fatalities every year.
Consisting of a phenyl group attached to an amino group, this organic compound smells like rotten fish and serves as a key precursor to polyurethane and dyes — what is it called?
Aniline: Organic compound (C6H5NH2); simplest aromatic amine.
Native to the northern tundra, this small mammal grows thick white fur for winter camouflage and forms monogamous breeding pairs while preying on lemmings and seabirds — what animal is it?
Arctic fox: Species of fox. It is well adapted to living in cold environments, and is known for its thick, warm fur that can be used as camouflage against snow in the winter.
This independent examination of financial records culminates in a report expressing an opinion on whether the books are free of material misstatement — what is it called?
Audit: Independent examination of an organization. The term is most frequently applied to audits of the financial information relating to a legal person.
First flown in 1947 with a distinctive V-tail, this single-engine aircraft holds the record for the longest continuous production run in aviation history — which model?
Beechcraft Bonanza: Family of single engine American light aircraft, first flown in 1945.

Despite its name, this snake is actually grey to dark brown — the name instead describes the dark interior of its mouth, displayed as a threat — which species, the second-longest venomous snake after the king cobra?
Black mamba: Species of venomous snake. The black mamba (Dendroaspis polylepis) is a species of highly venomous snake belonging to the family Elapidae.
Cattle, bison, buffalo, and goat-antelopes like sheep and goats all belong to this family of cloven-hoofed ruminants with over 140 living species — what is it?
Bovidae: Family of mammals belonging to even-toed ungulates.
In 1930, which Indian physicist won the Nobel Prize for discovering that light changes wavelength when passing through a transparent material, becoming the first Asian to win a Physics Nobel?

This polyatomic ion, CO3 with a 2- charge, is dissolved into water under pressure to make it fizzy, and also makes up much of the sedimentary rock in the Earth's crust — what's the ion (and salt) called?
Carbonate: Salt or ester of carbonic acid.
Discovered in 1945 and first sold in 1964, this class of beta-lactam antibiotics was originally pulled from a fungus once known as Cephalosporium — what's the family called?
This form of cancer that begins in the tubes carrying digestive fluid from the liver can cause yellowing skin, dark urine, and pale stools — what is it?
Cholangiocarcinoma: Cancer of the bile ducts.
Commonly called the tailbone, this bone is the vestigial remnant of a tail in humans and other tailless primates, sitting just below the sacrum — which bone?
Coccyx: Bone of the pelvis. In tailless primates (e.g. humans and other great apes) since Nacholapithecus (a Miocene hominoid), the coccyx is the remnant of a vestigial tail.
First created near Darmstadt in 1996 and named for an astronomer on his 537th anniversary, this synthetic element (number 112) is so volatile it may even be a gas — which element?
Copernicium: Chemical element with atomic number 112 (Cn)
Sold under trade names like Super Glue and Krazy Glue, this fast-acting adhesive family rapidly polymerizes the moment it contacts water — which chemical group?
Cyanoacrylate: Type of fast-acting adhesive. The cyanoacrylate group in the monomer rapidly polymerizes in the presence of water to form long, strong chains.
With evidence of practice dating back to 7000 BC, this field is considered the very first specialization to branch off from general medicine — what is it?
Dentistry: Branch of medicine. Dentistry, also known as dental medicine and oral medicine, is the branch of medicine focused on the teeth, gums, and mouth.
Nicknamed 'Spad' after a World War I fighter, this piston-engine attack plane flew from 1946 into the 1980s, an anachronism deep into the Jet Age — which aircraft?
Douglas A-1 Skyraider: American single engine attack aircraft.
Linked with orgasm and involving involuntary pelvic-floor contractions, this male bodily process can even happen during sleep as a so-called 'wet dream' — what is it?
Ejaculation: Semen discharge from the male reproductive tract.
This 1939 Nobel Physics laureate invented the cyclotron and went on to found two national laboratories that carry his surname today — who was he?

Scientifically known as Chloris chloris, this small finch is widespread across Europe, North Africa, and Southwest Asia, and has also been introduced to Australia, New Zealand, Uruguay, and Argentina — what bird is this?
European greenfinch: Species of bird. The European greenfinch or simply the greenfinch (Chloris chloris) is a small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae.
Historically used in the 18th century to track down escaped slaves, this large Brazilian dog breed of mastiff type now also serves as a guard dog and companion — which breed?
Fila Brasileiro: Brazilian breed of dog. The Fila Brasileiro (Portuguese pronunciation: [ˈfilɐ bɾaziˈlejɾu]) is a Brazilian breed of large working dog of mastiff type.

Coated in cornmeal and pan-cooked while still unripe, this dish was originally a Northeastern and Midwestern staple before a hit movie rebranded it as quintessentially Southern comfort food — what is it?
Fried green tomatoes: American dish. Fried green tomatoes is a culinary dish usually found in the United States, made from unripe (green) tomatoes coated with cornmeal and fried.

Working at Tuskegee Institute, this agricultural scientist urged cotton farmers to plant peanuts and sweet potatoes instead, publishing dozens of practical bulletins to fight soil depletion. Who is he?
George Washington Carver: American botanist and inventor (1864–1943)

This German engineer invented the high-speed petroleum engine, working alongside his lifelong partner Wilhelm Maybach to build small, fast motors they hoped to mount on any kind of vehicle. Who was he?
Gottlieb Daimler: German engineer, industrialist and automotive pioneer (1834–1900)
This protein filament that grows from follicles in the skin is one of the defining traits of mammals, and its removal or styling carries different meanings across cultures — what is it?
Hair: Protein filament that grows from follicles found in the dermis, or skin.
This field of study focuses on the methodological principles of interpreting texts — especially biblical and philosophical writings — and is closely related to exegesis. What is it called?
Hermeneutics: The study of the methodological principles of interpretation. As necessary, hermeneutics may include the art of understanding and communication.
In Greek myth, this fragrant spring bulb sprang from the blood of a youth slain by a jealous west wind god who coveted his bond with Apollo — what flower is it?
Co-creator of the AlexNet neural network and former chief scientist at OpenAI, this computer scientist has won NeurIPS's Test of Time Award three years running — who is he?
Native to Africa and Eurasia, this opportunistic canid can sustain a running pace of about 10 mph over long distances while hunting small mammals, birds, and reptiles — which animal?
A real estate magnate and Spanish–American War officer worth roughly $87 million, he was the richest passenger aboard the Titanic — and went down with it in 1912. Who was he?
John Jacob Astor IV: American businessman and Titanic passenger (1864–1912)
Derived from Greek words for 'movement' and 'study,' this scientific field examines biomechanics, motor control, and rehabilitation to understand how the human body moves — what field is this?
Kinesiology: Study of human body movement. Kinesiology addresses physiological, anatomical, biomechanical, pathological, neuropsychological principles and mechanisms of movement.
This genus of bacteria mainly infects amoebae but can cause a pneumonia-like illness in humans when it spreads via poorly maintained cooling towers — what genus is it?
Legionella: Pathogenic genus of Gram-negative bacteria.
Named after both a biblical sea monster and the author of 'Moby-Dick,' this extinct predatory sperm whale roamed ancient oceans roughly 9 million years ago — which genus?
Livyatan: Extinct genus of sperm whale from the Miocene epoch.
Marketed by Apple since 2001 for its line of Mac computers, this proprietary operating system derives from OPENSTEP for Mach and FreeBSD. What kind of system is it?
macOS, previously OS X and originally Mac OS X, is a proprietary Unix operating system derived from OPENSTEP for Mach and FreeBSD, marketed and developed by Apple since 2001.
The heaviest members of the squirrel family, these ground-dwelling herbivores live in groups through the summer before disappearing underground to hibernate all winter — what are they?
Marmot: Genus of mammals (large ground squirrels)
This rose-family shrub, commonly known as the medlar, produces fruit that's traditionally eaten only after it has softened past ripeness — what's its scientific name?
Mespilus germanica: Fruit tree, the medlar. Mespilus germanica, known as the medlar or common medlar, is a large shrub or small tree in the rose family Rosaceae.
Named for the Latin for 'thousand feet,' no species of this many-legged arthropod class was confirmed to have 1,000-plus legs until a 2020 discovery with over 1,300 — what are they?
Millipede: Class of arthropods. Its primary defence mechanism is to curl into a tight coil, thereby protecting its legs and other vital delicate areas on the body behind a hard exoskeleton.
Grown above the upper lip and below the nose, this facial hair style has taken many forms across history — what is it called?
Moustache: Strip of facial hair across the upper lip. A moustache (UK:) or mustache (US:) is a growth of facial hair grown above the upper lip and under the nose of men.
Divided anatomically into vertebral, visceral, and two vascular compartments, which flexible body part connects the head to the torso and is also called the cervix or collum?
Neck: Body part that connects the head and torso. It supports the weight of the head and protects the nerves that transmit sensory and motor information between the brain and the rest of the body.
Designed in the late 1950s as a six-engine, delta-winged prototype bomber capable of Mach 3+ at 70,000 feet, this aircraft was meant to outrun any interceptor of its era — which plane?
North American XB-70 Valkyrie: Prototype supersonic strategic bomber.
Found on every continent but Antarctica, these flowers can lure pollinators by mimicking female insects, and their tiny seeds depend on fungal partners just to sprout. What plant family is this?
Orchid: Family of flowering plants in the order Asparagales.
This term describes the bulk functional tissue of an organ like the brain or lungs, the filler tissue inside flatworms, and certain leaf cross-section layers in plants — what is it?
Parenchyma: Visceral tissue found inside organs of animals.
Discovered in 1972 and used to treat scabies and lice, this pyrethroid insecticide is safe for most mammals but especially dangerous to cats, who metabolize it slowly — what is it?
Permethrin: Medication and insecticide. It is applied to the skin as a cream or lotion.
Manufactured in Switzerland since 1991, this pressurized single-engine turboprop's large aft cargo door has made it popular with air-ambulance operators and police departments alike — which aircraft?
Pilatus PC-12: Swiss executive and utility transport aircraft.
Emerging in the 1960s as scholars from once-colonized nations began writing back, this academic field examines the lingering cultural and political effects of empire — what's it called?
Postcolonialism: Study of the cultural legacy of colonialism and imperialism.
Which medical specialty focuses on diagnosing, treating, and preventing conditions related to cognition, mood, emotion, and behavior, using tools like the DSM-5?
Psychiatry: Branch of medicine devoted to mental disorders.
Native to Southeast Asia and a close relative of the lychee and longan, this medium-sized tree lends its name to a hairy-skinned tropical fruit — what is it?
Rambutan: Southeast Asian fruit. Rambutan (Nephelium lappaceum) is a medium-sized tropical tree in the family Sapindaceae.
Extracted from the seeds of the castor oil plant, this lectin toxin carries an estimated lethal oral dose in humans of about one milligram per kilogram — what is it?
Also called false saffron, this thistle-like annual is one of the world's oldest crops, prized today for the vegetable oil pressed from its seeds — what plant is it?
Safflower: Species of plant. Safflower (Carthamus tinctorius), also false saffron, is a highly branched, herbaceous, thistle-like annual plant in the family Asteraceae.
This synthetic element, number 106, holds the rare distinction of being named after a scientist who was still alive at the time — its most stable isotopes survive mere minutes. What is it?
Seaborgium: Chemical element with atomic number 106 (Sg)

Usually triggered by a viral infection and common in people with asthma or cystic fibrosis, this inflammation of the facial mucous membranes causes congestion, facial pain, and loss of smell. What condition is it?
Sinusitis: Inflammation of the sinus' membranes. Sinusitis is a condition that affects both children and adults.

Starting from stem cells near the wall of the seminiferous tubules, this multi-stage process runs cells through two rounds of meiosis to turn diploid germ cells into haploid swimmers. What is it called?
Belonging to a fish family whose fossils date back to the Late Cretaceous, these long-lived, late-maturing fish share their order with paddlefish and once swam as far as North Africa — what are they?
Named after a figure from Greek mythology, this blue-gray transition metal with atomic number 73 is prized for corrosion resistance and shows up in capacitors inside computers. What element is this?
Tantalum: Chemical element with atomic number 73 (Ta)
This body region between the hip and the knee contains a single bone — the femur — that forms a ball-and-socket joint above and a hinge joint below. What is it?
Thigh: Body part between pelvis and knee; upper leg.
Also known as the windpipe, this cartilaginous tube linking the throat to the lungs is reinforced by horseshoe-shaped rings of cartilage — what is it?
Trachea: Cartilaginous tube. The trachea extends from the larynx and branches into the two primary bronchi.
Carrying the placeholder symbol Ubb, this hypothetical element 122 is expected to sit within the 'island of stability' — what is its systematic IUPAC name?
Unbibium: Theoretical chemical element with atomic number 122 (Ubb)

Most animals make their own, but humans, guinea pigs, and some bats must eat it because a synthesis-enzyme gene is broken; this citrus nutrient builds collagen and acts as an antioxidant — what is it?
Vitamin C: Essential nutrient found in citrus fruits and other foods.
Ranging from a few meters for Bluetooth to millions of kilometers for deep-space signals, this method of sending information relies on radio waves instead of cables -- what is it called?
Wireless: Transfer of information or power that does not require the use of physical wires.
Tellurium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for tellurium is Te. Tellurium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Te and atomic number 52.
Darmstadtium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for darmstadtium is Ds. Darmstadtium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Ds and atomic number 110.

Which of these is a comedian?
Jon Stewart is a comedian. Stewart is known as the host of the satirical news program The Daily Show on Comedy Central from 1999 to 2015 and part-time since 2024.
In what year was Jake Gyllenhaal born?
Jake Gyllenhaal: Gyllenhaal began acting as a child, making his debut in City Slickers (1991), followed by roles in his father's films A Dangerous Woman (1993) and Homegrown (1998).
In what year was Helena Bonham Carter born?
Helena Bonham Carter (born 26 May 1966) is a British actress.
In what year was Katherine Heigl born?
Katherine Heigl ( HY-gəl; born November 24, 1978) is an American actress and model.
